mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate below 3.5% triggers increased investor confidence in labor market strength, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns when UNRATE falls below 3.5% but negative returns in >70% of such instances (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rises in both personal consumption (GDPC1) and housing-related demand (HOUST) signal robust economic growth, amplifying equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and HOUST rise >5% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both GDPC1 and HOUST rise >5% from prior month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a sustained decline in the federal funds rate compresses discount rates, enhancing the present value of future earnings for equities and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regime, FEDFUNDS decline does not lead to positive 60-day returns in >60% of instances (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in production capacity (INDPRO) above 102 signals stronger supply-side growth, reducing production costs and boosting corporate profits, which positively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO crossing above 102 does not correlate with positive 20-day returns in >50% of cases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in employment (PAYEMS) above 157,232 (previous month's level) indicates strong labor market absorption, fostering optimism and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not positive when PAYEMS rises above 157,232 (prior month's value) in >70% of triggered instances (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in personal consumption (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their respective 5% monthly increases signals robust demand across sectors, elevating equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and INDPRO rise >5% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns not significantly higher than baseline when both GDPC1 and INDPRO rise >5% from prior month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market, a sustained drop in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals labor shortages, prompting investors to seek safer assets and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In tight labor market regime, UNRATE falling below 4.0% does not result in positive 60-day returns in >60% of cases (p > 0.05).
